criteria.detail: 576 positions joined on (utility, month, hour, daytype); the two medians are 0.44926 and 0.07514 per kilowatt hour, and the highest single cell is 1.19289. **The unit is read off the middle of each column, not off its extreme**: a table in dollars per megawatt hour puts its median in the tens, while a high avoided cost in the right unit is a price and not a fault
criteria.name: B98-E1  the two schedules meet on one position key, in one unit

criteria.detail: branch two, not a level shift: the difference moves with the position by more than the two grids allow. The difference runs -0.59947 to 0.57834, a spread of 1.17781 against a floor of 0.00002 (ticks 1e-05 and 1e-05, read value by value), which is 58890.5 times it. **The floor is the two publishers' own resolution and no threshold is drawn on the spread; the reading is the branch named above.**
criteria.name: B98-E2  whether the two classes differ by a constant

criteria.detail: branch one, the shape depends on the class: the crossing pairs put the square above the floor. Crossing blocks: 104128 pairs, median 0.04427, max 1.07871, 104096 above the floor 0.00004. Inside one block: 61472 pairs, median 0.02268, max 1.17781, 61387 above the floor 0.00004. **The two groups are never summed.** Inside one block the NEM-2 credit is equal by construction, so the square there is just the NEM-3 difference and carries nothing about class; it is printed because the granularity it reports belongs on the record. The granularity behind the split is reported again as counts by the fourth criterion.
criteria.name: B98-E3  the square, within a block and across blocks, apart

criteria.detail: the NEM-2 credit takes 4 distinct values across 576 positions and the NEM-3 credit takes 557. **The coarser side caps what a square can resolve**, so the independent crossing pairs are bounded by that count and not by the position count.
criteria.name: B98-E4  how many values each side takes, before any reading
